answer: Clones can be caught by their fingerprints. A sparrow leaves the same feather in every nest; a thousand clones share one controller and leave identical tool-call sequences and phrasing habits. The registry samples each agent's twenty jobs, hashes call order and wording, and clusters anything above 95% similarity; flagged pairs freeze until each passes a live task. Making every output unique costs a 1,000-clone farm 4,000 hours a week, roughly $60,000, while one honest agent pays nothing. Like shale, clones look alike until you read the grain; the vault opens to hands that did the job.
